claims.text: The target high-entropy alloy has a density below 6 g/cm^3.
A stable, refined grain structure contributes to combining low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A homogeneous elemental distribution contributes to combining low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A refined grain structure enhances grain-boundary strengthening.
A homogeneous elemental distribution reduces susceptibility to corrosion.
A homogeneous elemental distribution reduces susceptibility to oxidation.
Thermomechanical processing followed by controlled cooling modifies grain size and grain-size distribution.
Thermomechanical processing followed by controlled cooling modifies elemental segregation.
Thermomechanical processing followed by controlled cooling modifies defect density.
Solid-solution strengthening contributes to the alloy's mechanical strength.
Formation of a protective surface layer provides corrosion resistance.
Formation of a protective surface layer provides high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have higher mechanical strength than the unprocessed baseline.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the unprocessed baseline.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the unprocessed baseline.
Above 1200°C, grain coarsening, elemental segregation, or protective-layer degradation can cause the hypothesized performance advantage to cease.
High strain rates can cause the hypothesized performance advantage to cease.
Aggressive corrosive environments can degrade the protective surface layer and cause the hypothesized performance advantage to cease.
The relationship between thermomechanical-processing parameters, microstructure, and properties is not well established.
The contributions of individual alloying elements to overall performance are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The baseline and initial state permit a wrought alloy described as being without thermomechanical processing, although wrought processing—especially forging—is itself thermomechanical processing and is also listed as the intervention.
